chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him about a man who falsely accuses his wife. He said: “He is flogged, then the two are left together, and he does not perform liʿān with her until he says: I testify that I saw you doing such-and-such.”

key_terms.يَفْتَرِي: falsely accuses or fabricates a charge
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is flogged as a legal punishment
key_terms.يُلَاعِنُهَا: he engages in liʿān, the mutual imprecation procedure between spouses

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man accuses his wife of adultery without making a direct witnessed claim?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a husband who accuses his wife of misconduct. It states that he is subject to flogging and that liʿān does not proceed unless he makes a direct testimonial claim that he himself saw the act.
